outline.description: This chapter introduces the patents-in-suit, the relevant technology, the parties, and the procedural history leading to this appeal, including the jury verdict and post-trial motions.
subtopics: Overview of the '134 and '775 patents and their subject matter—methods for mitigating intermodulation product (IMP) interference in radios
Key technical concepts: intermodulation products (IMPs), passive intermodulation products (PIM), and the distinction between internal and external PIM
The parties: Finesse Wireless LLC as patent owner, AT&T Mobility LLC as defendant, and Nokia of America Corporation as intervenor
The accused instrumentation: Nokia radios with the PIM cancellation (PIM-C) feature
Procedural history: jury verdict finding infringement and validity, damages award of $166,303,391, and denial of JMOL and new trial motions
Appellate jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. § 1295(a)(1)

outline.chapter_title: Standards of Review for JMOL and Infringement Findings
outline.description: This chapter explains the legal standards governing the Federal Circuit's review of JMOL denials, jury findings, and claim construction, as derived from regional circuit law and Federal Circuit precedent.
subtopics: JMOL denial reviewed under regional circuit law (Fifth Circuit standard)
The de novo standard for reviewing JMOL denials: reversal only if evidence points so strongly in favor of one party that reasonable jurors could not reach a contrary conclusion
Substantial evidence standard for jury findings on infringement: whether a reasonable jury could have found for the prevailing party
De novo review of claim construction with clear error review of underlying factual findings
Abuse of discretion standard for denial of a new trial under Fifth Circuit law
The burden of proof: plaintiff's obligation to prove infringement by the accused device

outline.chapter_title: Noninfringement Analysis of the '134 Patent – Insufficient Expert Testimony
outline.description: This chapter details the court's analysis of the '134 patent claims, focusing on how the plaintiff's expert testimony failed to establish that the accused radios sampled both 'signals of interest' and 'interference generating signals' as required by the claims.
subtopics: Representative Claim 1 of the '134 patent and its six method steps
The critical limitation 1[a]: over-sampling a passband containing both 'signals of interest' and 'interference generating signals'
Dr. Wells' infringement theory: mapping 'signals of interest' to the downlink transmit reference and 'interference generating signals' to the modeled PIM path
The fatal timing problem: the modeled PIM path is generated downstream of the RF ADC after sampling occurs
Dr. Wells' contradictory and confusing testimony on cross-examination
The court's analysis: expert testimony must be clear and consistent, not self-contradictory
Application of Johns Hopkins Univ. v. Datascope Corp.: insufficient evidence when expert offers contradictory testimony on claim limitations
Holding: no substantial evidence supports the jury's infringement verdict for the '134 patent

outline.chapter_title: Noninfringement Analysis of the '775 Patent – The Seven Multiplications Requirement
outline.description: This chapter examines the '775 patent claims, including the claim construction dispute over 'three signals,' the prosecution history estoppel argument, and the court's finding that no reasonable jury could conclude the accused radios perform the seven claimed multiplications.
subtopics: Representative Claim 1 of the '775 patent and its method for generating IMP cancellation signals
Claim construction: 'three signals S1, S2 and S3' construed as 'separately identifiable' but not 'unique'
Appellants' prosecution history estoppel argument: claim amendment from 'two or three signals' to 'three signals'
Court's rejection of surrender argument: amendment did not constitute 'clear and unambiguous' disavowal under Continental Circuits
The seven claimed third-order multiplications: S1×S1×S2, S1×S2×S2, S1×S2×S3, S1×S1×S3, S2×S2×S3, S1×S3×S3, and S2×S3×S3
Evidence at trial: Nokia document showing only three distinct multiplications using modulus and complex conjugate operations
Dr. Wells' failure to explain how three multiplications map to the seven claimed multiplications
Finesse's flawed mapping argument on appeal requiring S3 to be mapped onto x2, its complex conjugate, and its modulus
Holding: no substantial evidence supports the jury's finding that accused radios perform the seven claimed multiplications

outline.description: This chapter addresses the damages award, explaining how the reversal of noninfringement moots the damages issues and results in vacatur of the monetary judgment.
subtopics: The lump-sum damages award of $166,303,391 for remaining patent life
Appellants' post-trial motions: JMOL on damages and alternative motion for new trial
Effect of noninfringement reversal on damages: vacatur as the logical consequence
Final disposition: reversal of JMOL denial and vacatur of damages award
Costs awarded to Defendants-Appellants
